To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a deep convolutional network architecture that combines a contracting path to captures context and an expanding path with learned, sub-pixel, spatial accuracy can be effectively trained end-to-end for segmentation using very few training images; (ii) the network can be trained to segment objects of varying size and at different scales from the same set of training images; (iii) the network can easily be adapted to segment objects in a new modality by training it on a single image of that modality

(1) a deep network architecture with a contracting path and a symmetric expanding pathway outperforms all other approaches to the ISBI challenge and (2) the same network architecture, trained on different data, is able to outperform all other participants in the ISBI cell segmentation challenge 2015 by a large margin.
